items.headline: SpaceX confirms about $40B of committed GPU financing, structured as an Apollo lease
items.summary: A filing on 26 October shows an Apollo-managed entity will buy Nvidia Vera Rubin chips and hardware and lease them to SpaceX for about 5 to 5.25 years, with leases starting in 1H 2027 and close expected by year-end. Rate and residual-value terms are undisclosed; this settles last week's unconfirmed Musk claim, with closing conditions still open.

items.headline: Anthropic's S-1 reveals Anthropic Direct: $125.2B of five-year leases on dedicated sites
items.summary: Filed publicly 26 October: third parties secure land and power and operate the sites while Anthropic leases them and buys its own accelerators; agreements began around 30 September. Total compute commitments are put at $542B to $567B, with counterparties and MW undisclosed.

items.headline: Anthropic's SpaceX deal is up to $120.5B but can end on 90 days' notice from early 2027
items.summary: The S-1 puts the deal at up to $120.5B through 2029 (Fortune). A newsletter's reading of the filings adds about $3.1B a month at full delivery in December, non-cancelable periods ending January and March 2027, then 90-day exits either way; those terms rest on that single source, as the SEC filing would not load.

items.headline: Microsoft's capex miss and Alphabet's cash burn hit neoclouds again
items.summary: Microsoft came in below expectations on 28 October and Alphabet posted free cash flow of -$9.1B against -$3.5B expected, and on 30 October CoreWeave fell 11% to $54.34 and Nebius 9% to $156.73. Evercore expects hyperscalers to burn about $200B over the next year; Nebius reports 12 November and CoreWeave 10 November.

items.headline: Australia's ASIC examines Firmus's failed float as chip payments come due
items.summary: Firmus pulled a A$44B float about two weeks before 29 October, when ASIC told a Senate hearing it is looking at what banks told buyers about demand. Filings suggest billions in chip commitments are in doubt, with US$550M due this year on one site and share handovers if it does not list by end-November; single source.

items.headline: Oracle's default insurance eases on a borrowing cap; Microsoft's $25B bond draws $115B of orders
items.summary: Oracle's five-year CDS fell 22 bps in a day to about 274 on 28 October after it pledged to limit new capital-markets funding to $20B through May 2030 (record 288 on 15 October). Microsoft's tranches then widened only 2 to 3 bps from issue, so top credit still clears; single source for the cap.

items.headline: JPMorgan note: $266B of AI bonds this year and CoreWeave CDS at a record 1,194.5 bps
items.summary: The 23 October note splits 2026 issuance into about $182B hyperscalers, $42B data center operators and $42B chipmakers, nearly double all of 2025, and says lenders now want proof of cash flow. CoreWeave's 2031 notes touched 16% before settling near 14%; read through a secondary summary, so treat as single source.

items.headline: Cipher's Barber Lake cost rises to about $13M per MW; new leases wait for 30-60% design
items.summary: On its 2 November call Cipher said cost rose from $10.4M per IT MW financed, with about $409M of tenant change orders of which only about $50M is reimbursed; a 20-year lease restores yield on cost to about 15% from about 13%. It is also building gas laterals for up to 2.5 GW with about 1 GW in early talks.

items.headline: Judge rejects xAI's bid to dismiss the Southaven turbine suit and its mobile-source defense
items.summary: A Mississippi federal court ruled 30 October that the plant is not a mobile source exempt from permitting, contradicting the state regulator's earlier view; it did not decide liability. An NAACP injunction request to halt the turbines is pending, and the state has issued a notice with about $6.1M in potential penalties.

items.headline: Argentina's country risk closes at 787 bps, up 180 in October, as external markets stay shut
items.summary: JP Morgan's index closed 30 October at its 2026 high, up 80 bps on the week and 385 from July's low, before easing to about 779 on 2 November. Analysts cite war, US long rates and a domestic recession, and say normal market access has not returned; EXIM may raise its Argentina line to $10B from $7B and DFC is studying about $20B, both ceilings rather than approvals.

kona: Offtake got a new door: Anthropic Direct means a lab now leases dedicated sites from third parties that bring land, power and operations, so Kona should pitch to it and to its build partners as a powered site, while assuming its 90-day style exit rights and pricing credit accordingly. Debt got harder: Argentina's country risk closed at 787 bps with external markets effectively shut, so a first financing needs an investment-grade or prepaid offtaker plus official money, and EXIM and DFC ceilings are the place to push, though they are not approvals. Cipher's 25% overrun and the Southaven ruling give two practical rules: freeze design before signing a lease, and get permanent air permits for on-site gas from day one.
stale: Kona tab, Argentina section: says country risk peaked at 655 bps and settled near 600 as a floor; it closed at 787 on 30 October, and the SpaceX case-study line citing 600 bps of country risk should move too. Players tab, SpaceX: the $40B Apollo-led package is described as sought; it is now a binding about $40B Apollo-managed lease commitment of 5 to 5.25 years, closing by year-end. Start Here point 2, Players and Financing tabs on the SpaceX deal: Anthropic shown at $1.25B a month and up to $84.5B; the S-1 now shows up to $120.5B. Players and Financing tabs, Oracle: record CDS of 288 is now about 274 with a $20B capital-markets cap through May 2030 (single source). Players tab, Firmus mentions: add the pulled float and ASIC inquiry. Kona tab, Argentina section: EXIM may rise to $10B and DFC is studying about $20B.
title: Anthropic leases its own sites; Argentina risk hits 787
